text:
ConocoPhillips stock rose 2.6% today to $137.56, building on a sharp nine-day rally that's seen the stock climb 9% since October 5. The immediate catalyst appears to be the gap between U.S. and global oil prices: U.S. crude is trading at $96 per barrel while Brent (the global benchmark) sits at $125—a $29-per-barrel spread driven by Middle East tensions, including Iranian nuclear developments and ongoing Saudi-Houthi conflict. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher global crude prices directly boost profits on barrels sold into world markets, especially as geopolitical risk premiums keep prices elevated.

The broader backdrop is a tug-of-war between supply concerns and relief. While the Trump administration's effort to allow Russian diesel into U.S. markets aims to ease the diesel crunch, traders and analysts have questioned whether it will actually bring meaningful price relief—meaning the geopolitical risk premium (the extra dollars investors pay for oil because of regional instability) looks sticky. That keeps crude prices firm for oil producers, supporting the stock's momentum over the past two weeks.
